findings.location: Section 3.3, 'Sign discrepancy in the PDF', last sentence; notebook EXP-3 markdown remark
findings.problem: The thawing remark says the Unite CPL curve 'and every attractive condensate' of EXP-3 'start phantom (w<-1) and cross w=-1'. For the condensate this is wrong twice. First, the document itself classifies the w<-1 epoch and the crossing as mean-field artefacts (Sections 4.6, 8.7, 12.3, 12.6: 'no state of positive-energy quanta of this Lagrangian is phantom'), but here it states them as fact. Second, even in the raw equations the history does not start phantom. Between the bounce and the zero of rho_psi, rho_psi < 0 and w = x0 sigma/(1+x0 sigma) > 1, so w<-1 appears only between the pole and the zero of M_eff.
findings.evidence: x0=-0.462654, bounce at a_b=0.720697 (fits.json): sigma=2.6714, x0 sigma=-1.2359, so w=+5.24 at the bounce. w stays above 1 until the pole at a=0.7734, is below -1 only for 0.7734 < a < 0.9745, and there M_eff < 0, which Section 8.5 calls outside the mean field's domain. The md line 58 sentence 'whereas both start phantom (w<-1) and cross w=-1' has no artefact qualifier.
findings.fix: Rephrase, for example: 'The Unite CPL curve starts phantom (w0+wa=-1.461) and crosses -1 at a=0.768. The condensate's equations give w<-1 only between the zero of rho_psi and M_eff=0, a region where the mean field is not valid (Section 4.6). Neither is a thawing field.' Make the same change in the notebook markdown.

findings.location: Abstract (line 7); Sec. 4.4 (line 110); Sec. 4.7 table rows 'kinetic energy' and 'phantom' (lines 145-148); Sec. 6.5 mixed-state bullet (line 263); Sec. 12.3 item 1 (line 689); Sec. 12.6 (line 785). The same claim appears in provenance/DIRAC16COMPLEX_STUDENT_GUIDE.md Sec. 6.10 (line 659) and notebooks/build_dirac16complex_notebook.py (lines 494-498 and 2339-2342).
findings.problem: The documents claim that no state of positive-energy quanta, or no positive-energy normal-ordered state, of this Lagrangian is phantom. As a general statement this is false. The argument rests on rho+p = S*M_eff and on 'KE_L >= 0 implies w >= -1'. Both hold only for the homogeneous k=0 condensate. For any state with momentum, KE_L = rho/2 whatever p is. Coherent Bogoliubov (squeezed) superpositions are ordinary states of the positive-norm Fock space, and EXP-4b itself produces them. In such states the normal-ordered pressure has a term linear in beta, while rho is quadratic in beta, so rho+p < 0 with rho > 0 at suitable phases. The same error leads Sec. 6.5 to dismiss the 2E pressure oscillation of the 'mix' runs as purely first-quantised. Take the Fock state in which one sea mode u_- is replaced by u = alpha u_- + beta u_+. Its normal-ordered expectation is u^dag B M u - u_-^dag B M u_-, and that expectation carries exactly this oscillation.
findings.evidence: The document's own EXP-4 formula (Sec. 9.5) is p_1 = (1-2|beta|^2)K^2/E + 2Re(alpha* beta) mK/E. The cross term is linear in beta, and eps has no cross term. I checked this independently with the fixture gamma matrices (scratchpad stage3_doc_tmp/physrev2/nec.py): m = K = 1, one sea mode rotated, pressure averaged isotropically (p = p_1/3), best phase. |beta| = 0.05 gives rho = 0.00707, p = -0.0224, w = -3.16. |beta| = 0.01 gives w = -16.5. |beta| = 0.10 gives w = -1.49. For incoherent number states the correct identity is rho + p = sum n (E + K^2/(dE)) >= 0, not S*M_eff.
findings.fix: Restrict the statement to incoherent occupation-number (Fock) states at Hartree level, with fixed normal ordering. Replace the derivation 'S M_eff >= 0 hence rho+p >= 0' by rho+p = sum n(E + K^2/(dE)) >= 0 for such states. State explicitly that coherent pair superpositions, which include the pair-creation state of EXP-4b, can violate the null energy condition transiently, as is standard in QFT. Base the 'mean-field artefact' verdict only on the argument that is actually valid: the occupied k=0 level becomes a negative-energy level when M_eff < 0. Reword Sec. 6.5 so the mix-run oscillation is not called unphysical.

findings.location: Abstract (line 7: 'mostly in the radiation era when H is of order m'); Sec. 9.5 bullets 'Production for m>0 only' and 'When the quanta are made' (lines 536-537); Sec. 9.7 (line 550); Sec. 12.1 (line 662); Sec. 12.2 (line 672); Sec. 12.6 (line 784). The same attribution is made in studies/dirac16complex_cosmology/src/exp4.rs (summary note, lines ~2311-2314) and notebooks/build_dirac16complex_notebook.py (line 2283).
findings.problem: The documents attribute the EXP-4b pair yields to production 'in the radiation era when H is of order m' and present them as a generic production mechanism of a few 1e-3 H_inf^3, largest near m = 0.5 H_inf. For m >= 0.5 H_inf the yield in the dominant momentum range is instead set by the instantaneous jump of Hdot (0 to -2H_inf^2) at the C^1 de Sitter/radiation junction. It is an artefact of how sharp the chosen transition is. A smooth transition, which NUMERICS_CONTRACT explicitly allowed, suppresses it by orders of magnitude. The quoted 'a third to a half at a=1' is measured in the first-order adiabatic basis, which by construction cannot see an Hdot jump at the instant it happens. It says nothing about when the physical production occurs.
findings.evidence: (1) I integrated the documents' own kink formula (mk/(4E^4))^2 over all k with the committed 64-node grid. It gives na^3 = 2.49e-3 for m=2 and 4.97e-3 for m=1, against the committed 2.421e-3 and 4.412e-3 (ratios 1.03 and 1.13). At k=2.67, m=2, pair_spectrum.csv has |beta|^2 = 1.203e-4 and the kink formula gives 1.156e-4. (2) I wrote an independent RK4 of the two-level mode (m sigma_z + (k/a) sigma_x) with Hdot = -2H^2 (1+tanh(t/tau))/2 (scratchpad physrev2/kink2.py, kink3.py). At tau = 0 it reproduces Rust: m=2,k=2.67: 1.20e-4; m=0.5,k=0.5: 2.346e-2 vs 2.353e-2; m=0.1,k=0.05: 0.2734 vs 0.2735. With tau = 1/H_inf the values become: m=2,k=2.67: 9.7e-10 (1.2e5 times smaller); m=1,k=1.5: 1.05e-6 (1100x); m=0.5,k=1: 4.8e-5 (78x); m=0.5,k=0.5: 3.0e-3 (7.7x). For m=0.1 at k=0.05 the change is only 1.2x (0.273 to 0.224), so light-field de Sitter production is robust.
findings.fix: State that for m >~ 0.5 H_inf the produced number, and the 'largest near m=0.5' ranking, are fixed by the discontinuity of Hdot at the junction and are strongly model-dependent. Only the m=0.1 low-k production is robust. Either add a smooth-transition (tanh-blend) run and report its yields, or label the current yields as sudden-transition upper estimates. Drop 'created in the radiation era when H ~ m' as the stated mechanism.

findings.location: Sec. 7.2-7.3 (EXP-2 'self-consistent' 8D Einstein cosmology; initial data line 315); also EXP-3 initial spinor (Sec. 8.3). Code: studies/dirac16complex_cosmology/src/exp2.rs initial_spinor (lines 345-362); scripts/check_dirac16complex_exp2.py has no such check.
findings.problem: EXP-2 integrates only the diagonal Einstein equations. By Stage 1 (ARBITRARY_FIELD line 960), T_ij (i != j) is proportional to (H_i - H_j) Psibar gamma^i gamma^j gamma^4 Psi. For the rest mode this bilinear is the spin density u^dag(i gamma^i gamma^j)u. In EXP-2, H_b, H_a and H_c all differ, so G_ij = kappa T_ij = 0 holds only if the (0,1),(0,2),(0,3) spin densities vanish. The (space, extra-time) pairs vanish automatically for B eigenstates. The same condition applies in EXP-3, where H_0 = 0 differs from H_a. Neither the documents nor any checker states or tests this condition. u(0) is described as 'the first vector' of a 4-dimensional eigenspace, as though any vector would do.
findings.evidence: From the t=0 rows of artifacts/.../exp2/run_x0_*.csv and the fixture gammas (physrev2/offdiag.py), the committed u0 has all 21 tensor bilinears u^dag B C gamma^i gamma^j gamma^4 u and all 7 vector bilinears equal to zero. The EXP-3 states are also unpolarised. The published runs are therefore consistent. However, a random normalised vector in the same (-i gamma^4 = +1, B = +1) eigenspace (physrev2/joint.py) gives (0,1) = 0.727, (0,2) = 0.517, (0,3) = -0.373. Such a state gives T_0j != 0 while G_0j = 0, so the diagonal ansatz fails for it.
findings.fix: State the consistency condition: the initial spinor must be spin-unpolarised in every plane (i,j) with H_i != H_j. The bilinears stay zero because u(t) is u0 times a phase. Add a Rust or checker check that these bilinears vanish. Note that the choice of u0 is not arbitrary. A Pauli-consistent state that fills all spin states per momentum is automatically unpolarised.

findings.location: Sec. 4.6 'Limits of the mean field' item 2 (line 137: Pauli caveat 'negligible for EXP-3 if the physical mass is of order eV or more'); Sec. 12.2 third bullet (line 673); Sec. 16.2 (line 892).
findings.problem: The eV-mass estimate is offered as a reassurance that the single-mode picture is Pauli-consistent for EXP-3. It leaves out that the Unite tuning also fixes the four-fermion coupling: lambda m^2 = 2 x0 (1+x0) m^4 / rho_psi0. In any mass range where degeneracy pressure is negligible, the contact interaction is then ultra-strong. Its scale |lambda/2|^(-1/2) lies below both k_F and m, far beyond any perturbative or NJL-critical value. The Hartree treatment with normal ordering against the free sea is therefore not self-consistent there. There is no mass at which both approximations hold.
findings.evidence: I used rho_psi0 = 0.695 rho_crit = 2.56e-11 eV^4 (h = 0.674), so rho_psi0^(1/4) = 2.25 meV, and x0 = -0.462654. Then lambda m^2 = -0.497 (m / 2.25 meV)^4, which is -1.9e10 at m = 1 eV. There |lambda/2|^(-1/2) is about 10 micro-eV, k_F = (6 pi^2 n / 8)^(1/3) is about 0.7 meV, and m = 1 eV. k_F/m < 0.1 needs m >~ 25 meV, which gives |lambda| m^2 >~ 7e3. |lambda| m^2 <~ 2 needs m <~ 3 meV, where k_F/m > 1. These are my order-of-magnitude estimates, not machine-checked outputs.
findings.fix: Add this as a further limit of the mean field in Sec. 4.6 and 16.2. The Unite-tuned coupling is outside the validity of a contact/Hartree description for every mass at which the Pauli caveat is negligible. Do not present the eV estimate as a reassurance for the attractive (x0 < 0) models; it applies only to x0 = 0.

findings.location: Sec. 12.6 'Dark matter: a qualified yes ... behaves like cold matter' (line 784); notebooks/build_dirac16complex_notebook.py (line ~2276, 'dark-matter-like (cold) behaviour').
findings.problem: EXP-4a is a free-streaming thermal relic that decoupled while relativistic (T_i = 10m). In the standard cosmological classification that is hot or warm dark matter. That its homogeneous equation of state tends to w -> 0 does not make it 'cold', which is a statement about its velocity dispersion or free-streaming length at structure formation. Sec. 12.2 item 5 itself concedes that free streaming was not computed.
findings.evidence: Sec. 9.7 describes the same gas as 'hot, then warm, then cold', and Sec. 12.2 item 5 says 'free streaming of the warm phase and clustering were not computed'. The 'cold' label in the final answer is therefore not supported by any computed quantity.
findings.fix: Replace 'behaves like cold matter' with 'becomes pressureless (dust-like) at late times', and state that whether the relic is cold, warm or hot depends on m, on the decoupling temperature and on free streaming, none of which was computed.

findings.location: Section 10.2 (nbconvert boxes, lines 1147-1160) and Section 14 troubleshooting table (lines 1452-1482); same command in notebooks/build_dirac16complex_notebook.py how-to-run cell
findings.problem: The nbconvert route can fail at kernel start with nbclient's default 60 s startup timeout. The guide's command does not set a startup timeout, and neither Section 10.2 nor the troubleshooting table mentions this failure or its remedy.
findings.evidence: In the fresh clone the guide's PowerShell box ($opts = "--output-dir","build/nbconvert","--ExecutePreprocessor.timeout=3600"; python -m nbconvert --to notebook --execute $nb @opts) exited 1 after 140 s: '[NbConvertApp] ERROR | Error occurred while starting new kernel client ... Kernel didn't respond in 60 seconds' followed by 'RuntimeError: Kernel didn't respond in 60 seconds'. The next step, check_notebook.py --also, then printed 'FAIL build\nbconvert\dirac16complex_dark_sector.ipynb: unreadable notebook JSON: FileNotFoundError' and 'FAIL cross-check'. The CPU was at 100% on all 24 logical processors from other runs. Rerunning the same command without changes passed in 614 s, and the audit printed all three 'ok' lines. grep finds no 'startup_timeout' anywhere in the guide, the notebooks or the scripts. Log: scratchpad/stage3_doc_tmp/asr/nbconvert.log (failure) and nbconvert2.log (pass).
findings.fix: Add --ExecutePreprocessor.startup_timeout=600 to both nbconvert boxes and to the notebook's how-to-run text. Also add a Section 14 row: symptom 'RuntimeError: Kernel didn't respond in 60 seconds'; cause: slow or busy computer, or first kernel start; remedy: rerun, or add the startup_timeout option.

findings.location: Section 3.1 table (line 87, 'Python 3.10 or newer'); also notebooks/build_dirac16complex_notebook.py line 256 ('3.10 or newer')
findings.problem: The stated minimum Python version, 3.10, conflicts with the pinned packages, which need Python 3.11 or newer. On Python 3.10 (for example the python3 of Ubuntu 22.04, which a reader of 'Linux (Ubuntu or Debian)' may have) the pinned pip lines of Section 3.5 and requirements-stage3.txt fail. The student then falls back to unpinned packages and loses the byte-identity results the guide promises.
findings.evidence: Installed package metadata (importlib.metadata): numpy 2.4.6 Requires-Python '>=3.11'; matplotlib 3.11.0 Requires-Python '>=3.11'. Guide line 87: '| Python 3.10 or newer | ... | yes |'. Section 3.5 pins numpy==2.4.6 and matplotlib==3.11.0.

findings.location: How-to-run markdown cell, lines 244-249 (rendered as cell 1 of notebooks/dirac16complex_dark_sector.ipynb)
findings.problem: The notebook's own setup instructions lead a macOS or Linux student into a configuration where the notebook's gauntlet is known to fail. findings.evidence: Measured in the clone: after 'rm -rf vendor/rustSolveIt; bash scripts/setup_solver.sh linux', a rebuild and '$bin all', git status listed exactly the 14 files of Section 4.5 (the ten EXP-1 K=0 and background files, the three EXP-2 CSV files and exp2/summary.json).
